title: Processing Human Colon Myenteric Plexus for Single Nuclei RNA-seq
author: Christina M Wright
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w26fghe
materials: Follow the instructions on the Qiagen RNeasy Micro Kit as detailed below:
Homogenize the lysate by vortexing for 30 seconds.
Discard the column and keep the flow-through.
Precool the Dounce homogenizer and pestles on ice.
Pre-cool large centrifuge to 4 o C.

steps.title: Prepare Sylgard Pinning Dish
steps.instruction: Prepare a specialized dish for tissue pinning using Sylgard polymer.

substeps.instruction: Combine Sylgard curing agent with polymer according to the kit instructions.
Drip Sylgard into a 35x10 mm dish until halfway full.
Allow to cure in a fume hood for at least 3 days.
Superglue the 35x10 mm dish to the center of a Fisherbrand Petri dish with a clear lid.
Insert more than 10 Minutien pins into the 35x10 mm dish.

steps.title: Prepare Krebs-Ringer Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of Krebs-Ringer solution using the specified recipe.

substeps.instruction: Combine the following reagents: NaCl (6.896g), KCl (0.343g), CaCl2·2H2O (0.368g), MgSO4 (0.1444g), NaH2PO4 (0.120g), D-(+)-Glucose (2.100g), and NaHCO3 (1.982g).
Add MilliQ water to 990 mL while stirring continuously.
Adjust pH to 7.4 using 4 N HCl.
Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 4-Di-2-ASP Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Create a 500 uM stock solution of 4-Di-2-ASP.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 9.8 mg of 4-Di-2-Asp powder into a 50 mL conical tube.
Combine powder with 50 mL sterile dPBS.
Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Pre-Arrival Setup
steps.instruction: Prepare equipment and reagents 30 minutes before tissue arrival.

substeps.instruction: Place chilling block in the -20 °C freezer.
Prepare room temperature, oxygenated Krebs-Ringer: Place ~20 mL in a 50 mL conical and bubble 5% CO2, 95% O2 using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Prepare cold Krebs-Ringer: Keep at least 50 mL at 4 °C (do not oxygenate).
Spray forceps and scissors with RNase Away and rinse/soak in water.
Chill methylbutane in a petri dish on dry ice by adding a few pieces of dry ice into the liquid.

steps.title: Tissue Reception and Initial Processing
steps.instruction: Receive human colon tissue and prepare it for labeling.

substeps.instruction: Transfer tissue on ice from Pathology in sterile 1x PBS in a 50 mL conical (~30 minutes).
Don PPE (gloves, lab coat, face mask, face shield).
Place tissue into cold Krebs-Ringer in a large sterile Petri dish.
Trim surrounding fat using Dumont #2 forceps and scissors.
Cut a ~1 cm x 1 cm piece of tissue and remove as much epithelium and submucosa as possible.
Transfer the small tissue piece (mostly muscularis) into the 35x10 mm pinning dish.
Add 2.7 mL of room temperature, oxygenated Krebs-Ringer to the tissue.
Pin the tissue flat, stretching it to maximum capacity.
Add 300 uL of 500 uM 4-Di-2-ASP stock solution and pipette up and down to spread evenly.
Incubate for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Cryomolds
steps.instruction: Prepare molds for tissue freezing during the 15-minute labeling incubation.

substeps.instruction: Label two Biopsy cryomolds as 'plexus' and 'muscle'.
Fill cryomolds halfway with O.C.T. and place on ice.

steps.title: Dissect Myenteric Plexus
steps.instruction: Isolate the labeled plexus under a fluorescent microscope.

substeps.instruction: Remove the 4-Di-2-ASP/Krebs-Ringer solution and replace with 2 mL cold Krebs-Ringer.
Place the 35x10 mm dish inside the larger petri dish filled with ice.
Place the assembly on a -20 °C chilled block on the stage of a fluorescent dissecting microscope.
Verify labeling in the 488 nm channel.
Using #5 Dumont forceps, carefully dissect away the muscle to expose the myenteric plexus.
Separate the plexus from surrounding tissue and place isolated pieces into the cold OCT in the 'plexus' cryomold.
Cut a piece of remaining muscle and place it in the 'muscle' cryomold.

steps.title: Freeze and Store Tissue
steps.instruction: Rapidly freeze the isolated tissue for long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: Place the 'plexus' and 'muscle' cryomolds into 2-Methylbutane in the fume hood.
Wait 5 minutes for freezing.
Transfer to a -80 °C freezer in labeled containment (e.g., plastic bags).
Clean plates with RNase Away and bleach.

steps.title: Section Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform cryosectioning to collect tissue for RNA quality control and nuclei isolation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 'plexus' cryomold on dry ice to a cryostat set to -20 °C.
Freeze tissue onto a metal mounting device using minimum O.C.T.
Chill Dumont #2 forceps in the cryostat.
Label three DNA LoBind tubes ('Plexus 1', 'Plexus 2', 'Plexus RNA') and chill on dry ice or at -20 °C for 3 minutes.
Make 100 micron sections.
Collect most sections in 'Plexus' tubes, but place 2-5 random sections in the 'Plexus RNA' tube.
Section through the 'muscle' piece to the middle and collect 2-5 sections in an Eppendorf tube labeled 'Muscle RNA'.
Return all tubes to -80 °C on dry ice.

steps.title: Extract RNA for Quality Control
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA from the RNA-labeled sections to assess quality.

substeps.instruction: Add 350 uL of buffer RLT plus to the 'Plexus RNA' and 'Muscle RNA' tubes.
Run through a gDNA spin column; centrifuge for 30 seconds at >= 8000 g.
Add 350 uL of 70% ethanol to the flow-through, mix by pipetting 4 times, and proceed immediately.
Transfer sample to an RNeasy MinElute spin column in a 2 mL collection tube; centrifuge for 15 seconds at > 8,000 RCF and discard flow-through.
Add 700 uL buffer RW1, centrifuge for 15 seconds at 8,000 RCF, and discard flow-through.
Add 500 uL Buffer RPE, centrifuge for 15 seconds at > 8000 RCF.
Add 500 uL of 80% ethanol, centrifuge for 2 minutes at 8,000 RCF, and discard collection tube.
Place column in a new 2 mL collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 5 minutes to dry the membrane.
Place column in a 1.5 mL collection tube, add 14 uL RNase free water to the center, and centrifuge for 1 minute at full speed to elute.
Analyze via Agilent RNA 2100 Bioanalyzer with Agilent RNA 6000 Pico Kit.

steps.title: Prepare Nuclei Isolation Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare dyes and buffers for nuclei isolation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Hoechst dye (2.5 mg/mL): Dilute 10 mg/mL Hoechst 1:4 in nuclease-free water, filter through a 0.22 micron filter, and store at 4 °C.
Prepare Diluted Nonidet P40 substitute: Add 1 mL RNase free Nonidet P40 substitute to 9 mL RNase free water and rotate for 30 minutes.
Autoclave large iridectomy scissors and Dumont #2 forceps after rinsing with RNaseZAP and MilliQ water.

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue for Nuclei
steps.instruction: Release nuclei from the frozen sectioned tissue.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Lysis and Staining buffers and place on ice.
Rinse large iridectomy scissors and Dumont #2 forceps with RNase Zap and MilliQ water; pre-cool on ice in a 50 mL conical.
Fill wells of a 6-well plate on ice with 6 mL Lysis buffer.
Transfer sectioned human tissue on dry ice to the bench.
Don PPE (gloves, lab coat, face mask, face shield).
Transfer one Eppendorf tube of sectioned tissue into 6 mL Lysis buffer in the 6-well plate.
Chop rapidly with large iridectomy scissors for 1 minute.
Transfer 2 mL of Lysis buffer + tissue/O.C.T. into a pre-cooled Dounce homogenizer.
Homogenize with 15 strokes of the loose pestle and 40 strokes of the tight pestle.
Pass the homogenate through a 30 micron MACS SmartStrainer into a 50 mL conical.
Chase with 2 mL Lysis buffer.
Repeat for all tubes from a single subject and combine in the same 50 mL conical.

steps.title: Purify and Stain Nuclei
steps.instruction: Concentrate nuclei and stain with Hoechst for FACS.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge Lysis buffer + nuclei + OCT at 590 RCF for 8 minutes at 4 °C.
Prepare collection tubes: 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes with 5 uL Staining buffer and Falcon round-bottom tubes (one per subject) on ice.
Carefully remove liquid from the 50 mL conical using a Pipet-Aid and P1000, leaving a small amount at the bottom to avoid losing the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Staining buffer by pipetting 5-10 times with a P1000.
Add 1 uL of 2.5 mg/mL Hoechst.
Strain the liquid through a FlowMi strainer into a spare Eppendorf tube using a P1000.
Strain again through the top of the Falcon round-bottom tube by placing the pipette tip flush against the strainer lid.

steps.title: FACS Sort Nuclei
steps.instruction: Isolate intact nuclei using fluorescence-activated cell sorting.

substeps.instruction: Transport samples and collection tubes to the FACS on ice.
Sort Hoechst+ nuclei into the collection Eppendorf tubes (containing 5 uL staining buffer) using a 70 micron nozzle.
Save the FACS program to document the isolation process.
Optional: Verify nuclei quality by combining 0.5 uL sorted sample with 9.5 uL Staining Buffer and viewing on a hemocytometer under an epifluorescent microscope.
Isolated nuclei are now ready for 10x GEM generation and library preparation using 10X Genomics protocols.
